--- title: "Mastering `ggplot2`" subtitle: "
36-315: Statistical Graphics and Visualization, Summer 2026" footer: "[36-315-summer26.netlify.app](https://36-315-summer26.netlify.app)" format: revealjs: embed-resources: true height: 900 width: 1600 theme: theme.scss smaller: true slide-number: c/t linestretch: 1.4 code-line-numbers: false html-math-method: method: mathjax url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" --- ## Topics * Plot composition * Colors * Themes * Annotations * Animations * Interactive figures ## Plot composition * Create the same type of plot many times * e.g., use faceting with `facet_wrap()` or `facet_grid()` * Combine several distinct plots into one cohesive display * e.g., use plot arrangement packages like [`cowplot`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/cowplot/vignettes/introduction.html) or [`patchwork`](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com/index.html) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) theme_set(theme_light()) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## Faceting by one variable ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + facet_wrap(~ species) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1344} ::: ::: ## Faceting by multiple variables ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + facet_grid(island ~ species) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1344} ::: ::: ## Arrange plots with `cowplot` * Example: shot attempts by the [Sabrina Ionescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Ionescu) in the 2023 WNBA season * Plot density curve and ECDF for shot distance together ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ionescu_shots <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qntkhvn/36-315-summer26/refs/heads/master/data/ionescu-shots.csv") ionescu_shot_density <- ionescu_shots |> ggplot(aes(x = shot_distance)) + geom_density() + geom_rug(alpha = 0.3) + labs(x = "Shot distance (in feet)", y = "Number of shot attempts") ionescu_shot_ecdf <- ionescu_shots |> ggplot(aes(x = shot_distance)) + stat_ecdf() + geom_rug(alpha = 0.3) + labs(x = "Shot distance (in feet)", y = "Proportion of Ionescu shot attempts") library(cowplot) plot_grid(ionescu_shot_density, ionescu_shot_ecdf, labels = c("A", "B"), label_size = 15) ``` ::: ## Arrange plots with `cowplot` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: ## Arrange plots with `patchwork` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} ionescu_shots <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qntkhvn/36-315-summer26/refs/heads/master/data/ionescu-shots.csv") ionescu_scoring_density <- ionescu_shots |> ggplot(aes(x = shot_distance, color = scoring_play)) + geom_density() + geom_rug(alpha = 0.3) + labs(x = "Shot distance (in feet)", y = "Number of shot attempts") ionescu_scoring_ecdf <- ionescu_shots |> ggplot(aes(x = shot_distance, color = scoring_play)) + stat_ecdf() + geom_rug(alpha = 0.3) + labs(x = "Shot distance (in feet)", y = "Proportion of Ionescu shot attempts") library(patchwork) ionescu_scoring_density + ionescu_scoring_ecdf + plot_layout(guides = "collect") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: ## Arrange plots with `patchwork` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} p1 <- penguins |> ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x = flipper_len, y = bill_len)) p2 <- penguins |> ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(flipper_len)) p3 <- penguins |> ggplot() + stat_ecdf(aes(bill_len, color = species)) p1 | (p2 / p3) & theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1344} ::: ::: ## Colors * **Discrete**: used to represent distinct categories with no ordering (nominal categorical). Colors should be distinct clearly with no single category emphasized unless intentionally highlighting a specific group * Do NOT use a discrete scale on a continuous variable . . . * **Sequential**: used when values are mapped to a single color gradient (e.g. choropleth maps), or for an ordered categorical variable or low to high continuous variable * Do NOT use a sequential scale on an unordered variable . . . * **Divergent:** used when data are centered around a meaningful midpoint and diverges in two directions from it (e.g., 0 for positive/negative values or 50% for percentages) * Do NOT use a divergent scale on data without natural midpoint ## Colors in `R` * Specify a color in `R` using * color name (see all with `colors()`) * hex code (see, e.g., [here](https://htmlcolorcodes.com/)) * `rgb()`: build a color using a quantity of red, green, and blue (+ transparency) . . . * Resources * [R Color Brewer palettes](https://r-graph-gallery.com/38-rcolorbrewers-palettes.html) * [Color palettes repository](https://github.com/EmilHvitfeldt/r-color-palettes) * [Color palette finder](https://r-graph-gallery.com/color-palette-finder) * [Working with colours in R](https://nrennie.rbind.io/blog/colours-in-r/) * [General color guide](https://www.datawrapper.de/blog/colors-for-data-vis-style-guides) ## Options for `ggplot2` color * Change discrete color palette with `scale_color_brewer()` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len, color = species)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){fig-align='center' width=864} ::: ::: ## Options for `ggplot2` color * Change continuous color palette using the viridis scales (also color-blind friendly) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len, color = flipper_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + scale_color_viridis_c() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){fig-align='center' width=864} ::: ::: ## `ggplot2` themes ::: {.panel-tabset} ### `theme_minimal`() ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ### `theme_bw`() ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + theme_bw() ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ### `theme_light`() ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + theme_light() ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ### `theme_classic`() ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ### Default: `theme_gray`() ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + theme_gray() ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ## Themes: ink, paper, accent * `ink` affects all foreground elements and parts of layers * `paper` affects all background elements and parts of layers * `accent` has niche application in `geom_smooth()` or `geom_contour()` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + geom_smooth(method = "lm") + facet_wrap(~ island) + theme_classic(paper = "cornsilk", ink = "navy", accent = "red") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: ## Theme components * For more customization, see [here](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len, color = island)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + facet_wrap(~ island) + labs( title = "Penguin Body Mass vs Bill Length", x = "Body Mass (g)", y = "Bill Length (mm)", color = "Island" ) + theme_bw(base_size = 18) + theme( # plot components plot.title = element_text(face = "bold.italic", size = 20, hjust = 0.5), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), axis.text = element_text(color = "navy"), axis.ticks = element_blank(), # panel/grid components panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "lightgray"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.border = element_rect(color = "darkgray"), # facet components strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightblue", color = NA), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), # legend components legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(face = "italic") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Themes from other packages ::: columns ::: {.column} * [`ggthemes`](https://jrnold.github.io/ggthemes/) * [`hrbrthemes`](https://github.com/hrbrmstr/hrbrthemes) * And many more... (see [here](https://github.com/erikgahner/awesome-ggplot2#themes-and-aesthetics)) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggthemes) penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + theme_gdocs() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Thinking about themes * Default choices tend to treat each element with equal weight * e.g., axes stand out as much as the data or background elements look the same as the points of emphasis * Design plot with the visual hierarchy in mind * Make elements of that are more important look more important * i.e., customize so that the data is the focus, not the axes and grid lines * Match visual weight to the focus of the graphic for communication ## Annotation * Use [`annotate()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/annotate.html) to manually add geoms (text, lines, rectangles, etc.) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} mtcars |> ggplot(aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point() + annotate(geom = "text", x = 4, y = 23, label = "Some text") + annotate(geom = "rect", xmin = 3, xmax = 4, ymin = 15, ymax = 20, alpha = 0.2) + annotate(geom = "curve", linewidth = 0.5, x = 4, y = 22, xend = 3.5, yend = 20, curvature = -0.3, arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(10, "pt"))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ## Storytelling with animation * Static version ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} f1_constructors <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qntkhvn/36-315-summer26/refs/heads/master/data/f1-constructors.csv") |> filter(name %in% c("McLaren", "Renault", "Racing Point"), year == 2020) f1_constructors |> ggplot(aes(x = round, y = points, color = name)) + geom_line(linewidth = 2) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 17, 1)) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Accumulated points", color = "Team", title = "The race for third place in the 2020 F1 season") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-28-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Animation with [`gganimate`](https://gganimate.com/) * Add a **transition** on top of the static plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} library(gganimate) f1_constructors |> ggplot(aes(x = round, y = points, color = name)) + geom_line(linewidth = 2) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 17, 1)) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Accumulated points", color = "Team", title = "The race for third place in the 2020 F1 season") + transition_reveal(round) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-29-1.gif){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## Key `gganimate` concepts * `transition_*()`: defines how data should be spread out and how it relates to itself across time * `view_*()`: defines how positional scales should change along the animation * `shadow_*()`: defines how data from other points in time should be presented in the given point in time * `enter_*()/exit_*()`: defines how new data should appear and how old data should disappear * `ease_aes()`: defines how different aesthetics should be eased during transitions See [here](https://goodekat.github.io/presentations/2019-isugg-gganimate-spooky/slides) and [here](https://slides.mitchelloharawild.com/wombat-gganimate) for great tutorials ## Considerations in making effective animations * Think about **pace**: speed of animation (too fast: hard to follow; too slow: boring and tedious) * Think about **perplexity**: amount of information; avoid information overload * Think about **purpose**: usefulness of animation (needed at all? providing additional value?) . . . * Always make and describe the static version first * Never add animation just because it looks cool * When presenting, make sure to explain what is being displayed in the animation and
which elements should be emphasized * This helps determine whether including animation is actually worthwhile ## Interactive plots with [**`plotly`**](https://plotly.com/r/) * Apply `ggplotly()` to a static plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} penguins_plot <- penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass, y = bill_len, color = species)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) + labs(x = "Body Mass (g)", y = "Bill Length (mm)", color = NULL) library(plotly) penguins_plot |> ggplotly() ``` :::
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
## Infographics versus figures in papers/reports * Infographics should stand alone: relevant labels, titles and captions within the plot

## Infographics versus figures in papers/reports * Figures in papers/reports should have captions explaining the information provided in standalone labels

Data sources: Transparency International & UN Human Development Report.]{style="font-size:83%;"} ## Resources * [`ggplot2` extensions](https://exts.ggplot2.tidyverse.org/gallery/) * [`ggplot2`: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis](https://ggplot2-book.org/) * [`ggplot2` website](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) * [`Mastering Data Visualization with `ggplot2` workshop at posit::conf(2025)`](https://posit-conf-2025.github.io/ggplot2/) (featuring latest `ggplot2` updates)

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
